summary:
Flamo is an SI-powered, voice-first fire-safety copilot designed to support astronauts, researchers, and learners throughout space missions. It combines an interactive 3D animation of different space environments, including an ISS-like spacecraft, a lunar base, and a spacesuit, with an intelligent SI companion that adapts its assistance to the user's surroundings.

Through voice or text interaction, Flamo serves two main purposes: providing crews with emergency fire-response guidance and mission assistance, while giving students, researchers, and engineers access to relevant scientific information, experimental results, and research findings.

Its intelligence is powered by a unified database integrating NASA's PSI combustion data and Combustion Science research. We connected scattered experimental records, NASA technical documents, and research papers into one queryable scientific knowledge base, making decades of microgravity combustion research accessible and interconnected.

Flamo uses this knowledge to retrieve relevant experiments, compare scientific findings with the user's environment, and present results through an interactive dashboard featuring visualizations, experimental data, and traceable NASA references. It also identifies research gaps rather than presenting unsupported conclusions.

MOTIVATION & OBJECTIVE


Motivation

Fire is one of the few emergencies a crew must handle alone, and the Moon base will make it harder. Apollo 1 was lost to fire in an oxygen-rich cabin, and both Apollo 13 and Mir survived oxygen-system failures. On Artemis II a smoke alarm went off about 80,000 miles from home. The atmospheres planned next raise the stakes: a Moon base or pressurized rover at 30% oxygen or more and 10.2 psi or less, and spacesuits at 100% oxygen and 4.3 psi.

NASA has decades of flight data on how flames behave without gravity, but it is spread across 24 PSI investigations, thousands of test rows in different formats, scanned data sheets, reports and papers. A researcher who asks "what burns near 34% oxygen at 8.2 psi?" must today open several tables and documents and reconcile units by hand. A student cannot easily learn why a microgravity flame is a sphere, or why that changes how fabric burns.


Objective

an SI-powered dashboard that summarizes, ranks and interprets the PSI combustion investigations for fire safety, in one conversation. Concretely, Flamo should:

  1. Find the investigations and tests that matter for a given habitat, atmosphere or question, and rank them by relevance.
  2. Extract comparable data (oxygen, pressure, flow, fuel, sample, outcome, spread rate, extinction) that supports predictive modeling.
  3. Interpret results in plain language, always with the source, and say clearly what the data does not cover yet (spacesuit atmosphere, partial gravity, Mars).
  4. Serve two audiences: a crew that needs a short, action-first answer, and students, researchers and engineers who need the evidence.

HOW IT WORKS

Solution Diagram

You ask Flamo by voice or chat. A router sends the question to NASA test data for numbers, or to NASA reports and papers for explanations. A checker makes sure every number is in the source. Flamo then speaks a short answer while the dashboard shows the evidence.

HOME

The user starts in the cabin hub and chooses one of 4 pillars: Prevention, Flammability & Fire Behavior, Detection, Suppression. Each pillar has sub-categories the user can click, or the user can just ask Flamo.

  • Prevention: Ignition, Materials
  • Flammability & Fire Behavior: Flame Spread
  • Detection: Smoke
  • Suppression: Suppression

Flamo Status

Flamo's face shows its state: Connecting, Idle, Listening, Thinking, Speaking, Disconnected. 

Dashboard

Ask by voice. Flamo answers and the dashboard updates 

KPIs and a chart, not just text

Every answer is cited

Ask by voice or text. Flamo speaks sentences, and the dashboard shows the full answer: KPIs, a chart, the nearest real tests, the most relevant investigations, gaps in the data, and numbered NASA sources that open at the cited page.

Scenarios

The same question, answered for the atmosphere you are in:

  • ISS (21% O₂, 14.7 psi): 221 tests in 8 investigations, High coverage.
  • Moon Base (≥30% O₂, ≤10.2 psi): 51 tests in 2 investigations, Medium coverage.
  • Space Suit (100% O₂, 4.3 psi): no test in the PSI data we integrated ran this atmosphere, so Flamo shows it as a gap instead of guessing. 
  • Custom: move the oxygen and pressure sliders, or just say “34% at 8.2 psi”. Flamo finds the nearest tests (29 here) and computes the oxygen partial pressure.


TECHNICAL ASPECTS

Data Pipeline Extraction

Two pipelines build Flamo’s knowledge.

Numbers

22 NASA experiment tables are merged into one test database. Gaps are filled from NASA documents only with an exact quote and page. Papers become 322 verified findings.

Explanations

Papers and reports are parsed by Docling. Text is chunked as is, tables are kept as tables, and figures by their captions. Everything is embedded (Cohere) into pgvector, tagged with its investigation and page.

Voice SI

Flamo is a LiveKit voice agent running Gemini Live. It doesn’t answer from memory: for every question it calls our server’s answer tool, which returns what to say and what to show. Emergencies take a fast path to a fixed checklist with no search.

Backend

A Python FastAPI server holds the answer engine. It reads the test database (SQLite), searches NASA reports and papers (Postgres + pgvector), reranks the results (Cohere), and serves NASA PDFs to the in-app viewer. Voice and chat use the same engine, so both give the same answer. 


How a Query Happens in the DB

The router reads the question and picks a path: data tools for numbers, or a search limited to the relevant investigations for explanations. The composer writes the answer, and a checker drops any sentence whose number isn’t in the source. Flamo then speaks and the dashboard opens.

TOOLS USED

Data Acquisition & Storage: NASA PSI, Python, SQLite, PostgreSQL, pgvector
Data Processing & AI: Docling, OCR, Gemini Flash-Lite, Groq, Cohere (Embed v4.0, Rerank) 

Voice AI: LiveKit, Gemini Live

Backend: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn 

Frontend & Visualization: React, Vite, TypeScript, WebGL, SVG 

Development & Deployment: Docker, Git, GitHub, Claude Code

IMPACT, LIMITS & FUTURE WORK

Impact

  • Crews: a fast, cited, action-first answer when time matters.
  • Researchers and engineers: comparable test data for predictive modeling, in one conversation instead of several tables and papers.
  • Students and professors: a way to learn why microgravity flames behave differently, with sources.
  • Mission planners and NASA: a clear view of where data is missing (spacesuit atmosphere, partial gravity, Mars), which helps decide what to test next.
  • Earth: the same insights support fire-safety technology on Earth. Fine-water-mist extinguishers developed for the ISS, smoke detection and firefighter gear all grew from this kind of research

Limits

Flamo is an educational and research tool. It is not flight-certified and supports, but does not replace, approved crew procedures. Its emergency checklist is a fixed, no-search path and would need review by fire-safety specialists before

any real-world use. There is no partial-gravity combustion data in PSI yet, and the challenge scope leaves out rockets and propellants. Where data is missing, Flamo says so instead of guessing.

Future work

  • Add partial-gravity results when LUCI and FM2 data appear in PSI. New investigations go through the same pipeline and appear in the same views.
  • Rank which missing test conditions matter most for crew safety.
  • Add data export so researchers can use the matched test data in their own flammability models.
  • Review the emergency checklist with fire-safety experts.
